problems.title: Gather or scatter

parts.prompt: Atomic updates in the scatter version?

problems.solution: 10¹⁰ interactions either way; scatter turns each into an atomic, gather into a register add.

problems.title: Coarsening reuse
problems.statement: A thread computes c consecutive x-points; per atom it loads 4 values and computes dy² + dz² once.

parts.prompt: Loads per atom–point pair for c = 1?

problems.solution: 4/c loads per pair. Registers and parallelism limit c.

problems.title: Time estimate
problems.statement: 10¹⁰ interactions, each about 10 FLOP-equivalents (including a reciprocal square root), on a 20 TFLOP/s GPU.
problems.solution: 5 ms: compute-bound, so coarsening and fast maths matter.

problems.title: Cutoff binning
problems.statement: Atoms uniform in a 100 Å box; cutoff 12 Å.

parts.prompt: Fraction of the box within a 12 Å sphere?
Speedup in interactions versus direct summation?

problems.solution: 0.72% of atoms per point: about 138× fewer interactions (minus binning overheads).

problems.title: MRI inputs in constant memory
problems.statement: k-space samples of 3 floats (kx, ky, kz) plus 2 for the complex value; 64 KB of constant memory.

problems.title: Fast maths accuracy
problems.statement: __sinf has absolute error about 2⁻²¹·⁴ for |x| ≤ π but grows for large arguments.

options: Compare the application's output (image quality, e.g. PSNR) against a full-precision reference

problems.solution: PMPP validates fast trig against image quality, the metric that matters.

problems.title: Register accumulation

options: accumulated in a register and written once

problems.solution: Register accumulation turns millions of writes into one.

problems.title: Few outputs, many inputs

parts.prompt: Problem with a thread per output?
options: Only 100 threads: the GPU is mostly idle
Split inputs across blocks and reduce partial results (split-K)

problems.solution: Split the input dimension and reduce: the same move as split-K GEMM.

problems.title: Arithmetic of a coarsened DCS
problems.statement: c = 4 points per thread; per atom: 4 loads, then per point 1 subtraction, 1 FMA (x² + d²), 1 reciprocal square root, 1 FMA (accumulate q·r).

parts.prompt: Instructions per atom per thread (loads + shared dy,dz part of 3 + 4 per point)?

problems.solution: 23 instructions per atom per thread, 5.75 per pair, versus 11 uncoarsened.

problems.title: Same structure
problems.statement: Which share DCS's "every output sums over every input" structure?
problems.solution: N-body, attention and KDE; vector addition is one-to-one.
